Response Text: Hey friends, Julie here. I-I wanted to take a second to talk about something important to me: this radio station.
I try not to talk about myself too much, but maybe you've heard me mention it before: I'm only 23, but I've had more than my share of bad times.
I-I don't say that to get you to feel sorry for me. I know that so many of you out there have had difficult lives too. Some far, far harder than mine.
I say it because I want you to know I can relate. I know what it's like to lose family and friends. To struggle.
But there's one thing that always kept me going, always meant something to me. It's this place. This radio station. This music.
These songs playing out across the world for everyone to hear...they mean so much to me.
They remind me of good times, of people I care about. Things that really matter. They offer...hope. I know it's cheesy, but hey it's true!
When I heard that people were coming back to Appalachia, I knew I had to make the trip. To find this radio station and make sure it stays running.
I'm not gonna act like it's mine, like, I own it or anything. I've fixed some times up, sure, but I didn't build Appalachia Radio. It doesn't belong to me.
But I want to make sure it stays on the air because...maybe it can give someone else hope. Maybe...Maybe that someone is you.
So, I hope you hear this music, and it makes you smile, or makes you think of someone you care about. That's what it's here for. That's what I'm here for.
...I guess I should probably get back to actually playing all that music I keep talking about, huh? Ha ha.
You're listening to Appalachia Radio, an enduring source of happiness in a sometimes unbelievable world.
One of the few things left in this world that hasn't been pulled apart for loose screws and circuit boards, this is Appalachia Radio!
Held together by duct tape, willpower, and a near-crippling fear of silence, this is Appalachia Radio.
From Clarksburg to Welch, from Flatwoods to Watoga, and everywhere in between, you're listening to Appalachia Radio!
Here at Appalachia Radio, I've recently gotten my hands on a Collectron. He is absolutely adorable, but has zero respect for personal boundaries.
[robot voice] Can I interest you in a block of concrete?
Oh my gosh, get OUT of here you big goofball!
You're listening to Appalachia Radio: It's like a Super Stimpak... for the soul. Hmm. That sounded better in my head.
The Andrews Sisters here have a great message for us all. Maybe some more'n others, if we're bein' honest... Lookin' at you, Crater!
Alright, can you imagine, three sisters all able to get along well enough to sing together? I wouldn't make it through a single song with my brother. No way! [laughs]
And now, here are the very prolific Andrews Sisters with "Straighten Up and Fly Right."
I feel like we're missing some pretty crucial information in that story. Why on earth would the monkey agree to that ride in the first place? That's what I want to know!
As soon as I hear that harp playing, I get all excited, because I know what I'm in for. It's really just kind of a perfect song, isn't it?
Next we've got Wouldn't It Be Nice... now isn't that a phrase we all say in our heads about a dozen times a day?
Break out your surfboards because here come the Beach Boys with "Wouldn't It Be Nice".
That was "Happy Days Are Here Again", which... well, hey. You're alive, ain'tcha? Pretty decent reason to be happy.
Here's one that might cheer you up on a rad-stormy day. Or serve as an excellent background for watching someone fall down repeatedly.
In my humble opinion, if you're in the right frame of mind then they're all happy days.
Oh, now this next song is one of my favorites. Just a sweet reminder that there are things out there that are worth livin' for.
Doesn't Billie Holiday just have the most beautiful voice? Every time I've heard that song, since I was a little girl, just been carried away by it.
Coming up next is "Crazy He Calls Me". If you ask me, the only thing crazy about Billie Holiday is how amazing her voice is!
Take a page from Billie Holiday, and believe you can do the impossible. It can make all the difference.
Well Mr. Bing Crosby, you would have loved Appalachia. More wide open land than you can shake a...mildly irradiated stick at.
Well this one pretty much sums it up for me. Here's Bing Crosby backed up by the Andrews Sisters with "Don't Fence Me In".
This next one goes out to all you Dwellers looking for the perfect, and I mean perfect, spot for your camp. It's Bing Crosby, singing "Don't Fence Me In".
Remember, ladies: just 'cause Bing Crosby tells you to put down the gun, doesn't mean you have to!
There's been a few times in my life I needed to pick up a gun, and every single one of 'em, this next song went through my head.
The Andrews Sisters and Bing Crosby are back again! This time with "Pistol Packin' Mama".
These days, you're likely to run across a Pistol, Combat Shotgun, Super Sledge, Gauss Rifle, Gatling Gun Packin' Mama. You can never be too prepared!
Mr. Johnson lays it out pretty clear doesn't he? Regardless of circumstances, the choices we make are what really matter.
Here's the best lesson about personal responsibility set to slide guitar that you'll ever hear. "Nobody's Fault But Mine" by Blind Willie Johnson.
Next, Blind Willie Johnson struggles with accountability in "Nobody's Fault But Mine".
I really like this song, but sometimes I'm reminded that this idea goes both ways. You can be presented with the worst of circumstances but still make the right choice. It's up to you!
Those "dear hearts" and "gentle people" are out there, everyone. And wherever they are, that's where home is. Don't forget that, okay?
Dear Hearts and Gentle People is coming up next. This one always makes me smile. Thinking about the people in my life who fit that description.
Whether Appalachia has always been your home, or you're a more recent arrival, this next song is for you.
That, my friends, was Bob Wills. Don't be a Bob, and sit around feeling sorry. Get back out there. Do something! Build a camp! Start a trading business! You can do it! I believe in you!
Hey there! Would you like to weirdly feel happy AND sad at the same time? Well here's your chance - it's "Bubbles In My Beer".
Here's a nice happy sounding song, as long as you don't listen to the lyrics. It's Bob Wills singing "Bubbles In My Beer".
...I really wish I knew how to play steel guitar. I'm working on the tuba, but that's... well, let's just say it's coming along, but very slowly. And loudly.
I hope you weren't doing anything important because it's time to dance! Here's "Steel Guitar Rag" by Bob Wills.
I hope that song is some good inspiration for any of you out there playing the steel guitar. It's got such a great sound.
Here's "Steel Guitar Rag". Like Bob Wills says, "Kick it off, Leon!"
Oh Cass, sweetie, raise your standards just a little bit! You're worth it! Well, it's a fun tune anyway.
So... I can't say I totally agree with Cass Daley on this, but let's just say if you find good people out there in the world, do what you can to stick with them.
Is a good man hard to find? I haven't been looking. You know what IS hard to find? Ballistic fiber! Oh my gosh.
Now we've got Cass Daley, with "A Good Man Is Hard to Find".
I love that one because it sounds like a bunch of friends just hanging out and having a good time. Insect phobias aside, of course.
Dad always used to ask if I had ants in my pants when I couldn't sit still. I guess maybe Chick Webb's dad did the same thing, since here he is singing about it.
You know that song is from a long time ago, because these days you couldn't fit more than one ant in your pants. And you definitely wouldn't want the pants back afterwards.
If you've been looking for a good groove so you can get up and move, here it is! It's "I Can't Dance, I Got Ants In My Pants" by Chick Webb.
I have been some places that would probably quality as "madhouses" and they are nowhere near as entertaining as that song. Just saying.
Here comes Chick Webb with a really fun instrumental called "Midnite in a Madhouse".
I bet we've all known at least a few friends who have lived life by the motto of "When I Get Low, I Get High", right?
Given the state of things, this song can be a convenient excuse to, shall we say, over-indulge. Moderation, friends! It's all about moderation!
I am in no way suggesting you take this song completely literally. But well, do what you got to do friends. Huh, here's "When I Get Low I Get High".
Bet you ten caps you can guess this next song within the first three seconds!

Coming up next is "Mr. Sandman" by the Chordettes. I guess I'd wish for someone, too... if I didn't have to worry about radiation, disease, ticks the size of my head, Scorchbeasts... you get the idea. Anyway, fun song!
Isn't that one a classic? I feel like everyone knows the first few lines then after that they're um and just mumbling along, not knowing the rest of the words. Huh, always fun to see.
You think Cole Porter would be surprised by where the world ended up since writing that song? Hmm, I figure he'd shrug his shoulders and say "Yeah, why not."
I'm not saying you all owe me, but when I got here the equipment was days away from breaking down. You were all saved from hearing this song, and only this song, repeating endlessly forever.
Do you think at any point those guys said "hey, this is kind of a weird thing to write a song about", because I wonder about it all the time.
Next up, looks like the Commodores with "Uranium." Bop along if you like.
Okay everyone. Here it comes! Grab your pals, maybe a banjo, and belt it out along with the radio. I know you've been waiting for this one.
Terminals here in the station say this was the most popular song pre-war. I can't take a real survey, but I'm betting it's still true today. Here is "Country Roads".
I still get goosebumps, every time I hear it. You do too, don't you? Aww, I know you do.
Stimpaks won't heal these burns. Here comes the "Ring of Fire".
Is there anybody out there who hasn't been burned by love? Maybe if you've been locked in a Vault by yourself... Gosh, now that I think about it, which is worse?
I feel like that could have gone on for another twenty minutes of solos, and it sure sounds like everyone playing would have loved doing it.
Get ready, because here comes Count Basie with "Jumpin' At the Woodside".
I just love that someone somewhere decided that the phrase "Bingo, Bango, Bongo" was worth using as a lyric. I hope it makes you smile too.
This song used to crack me up as a kid. And it sure sounds like they had fun recording it. It's the Andrews Sisters with Danny Kaye singing "Civilization".
Just a friendly reminder to look after your neighbors, everyone. We're all in this together, after all.
Haven't seen "Ol Man Mose" around lately? Welllll, here's why!
Wondering what's up with Ol' Man Mose? Here's Eddy Duchin to fill you in.
If no one ever told you, it's bad manners to stare in your neighbor's windows. Yes even if they're dead.
And now for something with just a little bit more 'twang', here's "Walking the Floor Over You" by Ernest Tubb.
[sigh] Lost love. Is there a more significant source of inspiration for music? I think not my friends. Let's hope you all fare better than Mr. Tubb.
Hope that you all enjoyed that one, friends, and that you're all on your best behavior too.
Oh, ok my brother Matty as a kid, oh boy, did he laugh at Fats Waller blurting out, "Believe me"! [laughs] Oh Matty, uh, wherever you are I hope you can hear this and I hope you're still laughing.
Oh, do I relate to this one. Just me and the radio, here by myself, got nearly everything I love within arm's reach. Here's "Ain't Misbehavin".
I-I mean I'm sure they meant it as a compliment, but I dunno, something about comparing your girl to an explosive device that can destroy the world...I-I [sighs] y-you see what I'm saying right?
Here's the Five Stars with "Atom Bomb Baby", a song that suggests they may not have made the most responsible choices when it came to relationships...
That was, if you hadn't picked up on it, "Mister Five By Five". I always feel just a little bad for the poor guy that song was about, but it sounds like he was a pretty good dancer, so good for him.

Up next it's "Mister Five by Five". Did you know this song was written about a real person? I can't remember his name, but he sang for Count Basie. Hmm, not sure this is how I want to be remembered...

What would the modern equivalent of this be? "Deathclaw Steak Pete"? Doesn't quite have the same ring to it... "Mutt Chops Pete"? Nah, that just sounds like you're making fun of his face... I'll keep working on it, friends.
I've heard some of you Dwellers tickling the ivories, but can you keep up with "Pig Foot Pete"? Here's Freddie Slack and Ella Mae Morse.
If I'm gonna make up a nickname for someone I really like and/or admire, I'm probably not gonna go with "Pig Foot" or anything of the sort. [laughs] What do you think friends?

Okay, so am I an awful person? I was thinking about this next song, "Two Left Hands" and how it's just figurative, only... maybe now there are a few folks out there with two left hands. Like, literally. And then I laughed. A lot. And now, while the song plays, I will feel bad for laughing.
I can't be the only one who wants to see a duet between Mr. Two Left Hands here and Pig Foot Pete, right? Who's with me?
Coming up next, it's Freddie Slack and his orchestra with "Two Left Hands".
Did you crack open a Nuka-Cola for that? I sure did. Also I am running super low on Nuka-Cola. Donations are appreciated.

I don't know about you all, but being a kid, sipping a Nuka-Cola, and dancing around the camp listening to this song, there's no feeling like it. Makes me happy every time I hear it. Here's "Juke Box Saturday Night".
It's a tough world out there, and you can't always count on everyone. Here's Henry King and his orchestra with "Just a Fair Weather Friend".
I'll say this friends: it's true that there are people in the world who will let you down, but it should just make you appreciate the folks who are always there for you even more.
Not everyone is a fair weather friend. You find the people who are there for you no matter what, and you stick together!
It's a good message, friends. Keep things small, simple. Focus on the good things, the things that really matter. Oh goodness, I-I'm such a broken record.
I Don't Want to Set the World on Fire is next, and don't worry Ink Spots. Someone already beat you to it!.. [laughs] Too much? Too soon? Sorry.
I know things might seem bad, but don't give up! Despite what the Ink Spots say, it's NOT all over but the crying. Heck, keep going and cry while you do it! Multitask!
Hello, friends. I'm Julie, this is Appalachia Radio, and these are the Ink Spots, singing "It's All Over But the Crying".
Well, that one sure is a classic. Hope you enjoyed it!
That song is just so timeless. Feels like it's been around forever, doesn't it?
Next up it's the Ink Spots, singing "Maybe." I have known and loved this song my whole life! I hope you love it too.
So it seems that sitting around, pining for your lost love, leaves you plenty of time to write songs about it! [laughs] Here are the Ink Spots with "Maybe".
Remember friends: you're not alone out there. The world is filled with people, and you share the same goals with at least some of them. Take care of yourselves. And each other. Okay?
Here's a song about the three people you can always rely on: Me, myself and I. [laughs] It's "We Three" by the Ink Spots.
Dear Ink Spots: I admire your commitment, but I think at this point it's probably just better if you, you know, move on.
Some of you Dwellers who are good with musical instruments, you should get together and learn that one. What a fun tune!
I don't claim to fully get what this song is about, but I do claim to have cleared some space in the studio here for dancing. I suggest you do the same! Here's "Doin' The Uptown Lowdown."

Doesn't that song sort of describe Appalachia these days? Whole bunch of people, different folks getting together to party? Of course, huh, the definition of "party" varies like a lot. [laughs] Still though!
Mister Jerry Irby would have just loved Nuka Shine. It's like ALL the nails, and the coffin, and everything, you included, shoved into a blender. [laughs] And that's IF you remember any of it.
If drinking to excess is your biggest vice these days, you're still better off than a whole lot of people. No judgments here, friends!
Let's call this one a cautionary tale about self-destructive behavior. I'm not telling you how to live your lives, just trying to help you live your best ones. Here's Jerry Irby.

Here comes "Headin' Down the Wrong Highway" by Johnny Bond. And Johnny, as long as that highway isn't overrun with Super Mutants or Feral Ghouls, it could be worse, buddy.
What do we think, friends? Is Johnny here being too hard on himself? Sounds about average for the folks I know!
No matter where you are, friends, you can always change course. It's never too late!

I know it's not the same for everyone, but for me, there are moments where I miss where I came from, and the family and friends no longer with us. Be grateful for what you have, friends, but don't forget where you've been.
In case you were wondering, Haile Selassie was actually a ruler in Ethiopia way back when. Huh, don't let anyone tell you listening to the radio is a waste of time - it's educational!
Here's a song near and dear to my heart, reminding us that we carry with us the places and people from our past. It's "In a Shanty in Old Shanty Town".
That one goes out to anyone that may, now or in the near future, be fending off an angry Scorchbeast. Good luck!
I wish I knew the story behind this next song because it was written so long ago, but it's so appropriate pretty much every day in Appalachia. Here is "Praise the Lord and Pass the Ammunition!"

I think I can speak for most of us when I say: We've known a Miss Effie or two in our time. They never learn do they?
The sound of that little gun going off makes me laugh every single time. Every time! Thank you, Ms. Montana.
Here's Patsy Montana explaining how to get away with murder? [laughs] "I Didn't Know The Gun Was Loaded".

Butcher Pete: how much should we read into this song? You make the call!

I'm sorry, what's that? It's a metaphor? Ohh, you don't say!
